name: Pooram Sound Society
tagline: Mayilpeeli College's music and band society, from chenda to distortion pedals.
about:
Pooram Sound Society is the music and band society of Mayilpeeli College of Arts and Science in Thrissur. We take our name from the city's great festival, where hundreds of percussionists and an ocean of people somehow land on the same beat. On a good day, that's what a college band rehearsal feels like too.

We have about 140 members: Carnatic violinists, a beatboxer from first-year Physics, three bands that rehearse in rotation in the old NCC room, a choir, and an increasingly serious chenda ensemble that practises behind the canteen at six in the morning so nobody can complain. Nobody auditions to join. You come to an open jam, you play or sing or just listen, and you keep coming back.

Our year has three big moments: Sruthi Night in the open-air theatre, the inter-college Battle of the Bands, and a monsoon unplugged session on the library steps. In between, members teach each other: guitar basics on Mondays, Carnatic vocal on Wednesdays and home recording on Saturdays.

Alumni bands still come back to play, and the canteen chechi can now tell a capo from a clothes peg. We consider both of these our greatest achievements.

events.name: Monsoon Unplugged on the Library Steps

venue.name: Library steps, Mayilpeeli College
venue.address: Mayilpeeli College of Arts and Science, Ollur, Thrissur

events.about:
Every July, when the rain settles in for good, we carry two acoustic guitars, a cajón, a harmonium and the choir out to the library steps and play until the light goes. No amplifiers, no stage, no setlist printed in advance. People sit on the steps under umbrellas, someone always brings a flask of chukku kaapi, and the songs follow the mood of the rain.

This year eleven acts played: the choir's four-part version of a 1970s film melody, a first-year duo doing Tamil indie, the chenda ensemble playing softly for once, and an alumni band who drove down from Kochi in a borrowed car. When the downpour got serious at 6:15, everyone moved under the library portico and kept singing.
events.guidelines: Free and open to everyone on campus and their friends. Bring an umbrella and something to sit on. If you'd like to play, sign up in the form; acoustic only, two songs per act. Please keep the steps clear for the library staff leaving at five.

speakers.bio: Graduated in 2021 and has driven back for every monsoon session since, usually with a broken string.

events.name: Sruthi Night 2026

venue.name: Open-air theatre, Mayilpeeli College
venue.address: Mayilpeeli College of Arts and Science, Ollur, Thrissur

events.about:
Our biggest night of the year. Sruthi Night opened with forty-two chenda players thundering through the open-air theatre, moved through the choir and all three of our bands, and ended past ten with the alumni band Paddy Field Radio playing songs the whole crowd somehow knew. The sound was run by students, the lights were run by students, and the dosa stall was run by the Commerce department, which made a profit.

Tickets were ₹150 for guests from outside the college and covered the sound hire. Every rupee left over went to repairing the drum kit and buying the choir a proper set of microphones.
events.guidelines: Ticket holders enter through the main gate from 5:30; carry your ticket and a photo ID. No outside alcohol or smoking anywhere on campus. The theatre is open-air, so the show goes on in light rain; we'll message everyone if it has to stop. Earplugs are available at the sound desk for anyone near the chenda.

speakers.name: Sachin Ravunni

Proud of the student sound crew. It sounded better than some paid shows.

events.name: Home Recording on a Hostel Budget

venue.name: Seminar Room B, Mayilpeeli College
venue.address: Mayilpeeli College of Arts and Science, Ollur, Thrissur

events.about:
You don't need a studio to make a song people will want to hear twice. You need a quiet corner, one decent microphone, free software and a few habits that most people learn the hard way. Nandakishore has mixed three indie albums from a converted cowshed in Ollur, and he spent this Saturday showing us exactly how.

We recorded a vocal in a hostel wardrobe lined with blankets, a guitar in the stairwell, and a chenda from the far end of the corridor. Then we mixed it all on laptops, compared versions, and learned why the first ten minutes of a mix decide everything. By four, the room had one finished song, which Chakka Radio played the following week.
events.guidelines: Bring a laptop with a free audio editor installed (the list is in your confirmation) and wired headphones. If you have a microphone or audio interface, bring it; we have six to share. The fee covers lunch and the studio's equipment hire.

events.name: Open Jam: First Years Welcome

venue.name: Old NCC Room, Mayilpeeli College
venue.address: Mayilpeeli College of Arts and Science, Ollur, Thrissur

events.about:
This is how everyone joins Pooram Sound Society. Walk in, pick up something (a guitar, the keyboard, a pair of chenda sticks, a microphone) or just sit on the floor and listen. The band members will play along with whatever you start, and the choir will try to harmonise with it. By the end of the evening you'll know who plays what and which band has room for you.

No audition, no experience needed, and nobody will ask you to play a scale. If you've only ever sung in the shower or at a family wedding, you are exactly who this is for.
events.guidelines: Bring your own instrument if you have one; we have two guitars, a keyboard, a cajón, a drum kit and the chenda to share. Shoes off inside the jam room. Please let quieter people have a turn at the microphone too.

speakers.name: Ashin Joseph
speakers.bio: Will play bass under any song you start, including ones he's never heard.

speakers.name: Haritha Unni
speakers.bio: Can find a harmony for anything, and will teach you yours in about four minutes.

events.name: Battle of the Bands: Inter-College Prelims

venue.name: College Auditorium, Mayilpeeli College
venue.address: Mayilpeeli College of Arts and Science, Ollur, Thrissur

events.about:
Twelve college bands from across central Kerala, fifteen minutes each, one shared backline and two judges who have heard it all. The top four go through to the finals in January, when the auditorium doors open to the whole city. Original songs earn extra marks; covers are welcome, but tell us what you did to make them yours.

The audience is free to attend and very much part of it: there's an audience vote for the band that best owns the room. Previous winners include Third Bench, who still mention it in every introduction.
events.guidelines: Bands: register the band leader here, then send the member list and a rough recording through the band form linked in the confirmation. Fifteen minutes on stage, including your line check. Audience: free entry, seats on a first-come basis, and no flash photography during sets.

speakers.name: Meera Raghavan
speakers.bio: Has trained singers for reality shows and church choirs alike, and judges on breath control before anything else.

speakers.name: Aneesh Pallath
